posts.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Why I’m Using OpenClaw to Reclaim my Academic Life – The Burden of the “Invisible Curriculum”
posts.content:
As a University Lecturer, my primary mission is mentorship and research. However, the reality of the academic day is often consumed by “cognitive load”, the relentless administrative friction that drains mental energy.

Recent 2025 reviews highlight that overwhelming administrative demands are a primary driver of emotional exhaustion. For academic clinicians, administrative interaction is the leading source of burnout (51%), far outstripping the stress of patient care (26.4%) or teaching (11.7%). With nearly a quarter of our working hours swallowed by paperwork, the risk to career longevity and teaching quality is systemic. Ironically, even traditional automation often adds “learning costs” and digital compliance hurdles rather than true relief.

Enter OpenClaw: The “Linux of the AI Era”
This is where OpenClaw offers a transformative shift. Unlike traditional chatbots that simply generate text, OpenClaw is an agentic framework designed for autonomous execution. It isn’t just a tool; it’s a digital teammate capable of planning and completing multi-step operational workflows.

For those of us in Health Professional Education, the potential is vast. Imagine an agent integrated with WhatsApp, Telegram, or Discord that can:

  • Autonomously triage inboxes and manage clinical placement scheduling.
  • Handle repetitive student FAQs regarding course prerequisites.
  • Reduce administrative queries by up to 70%, potentially reclaiming 5 to 8 hours of faculty time every week.

In the rapidly evolving academic landscape of Hong Kong, adopting these agentic systems isn’t just a luxury; it’s a definitive step toward future-proofing the educator’s role.

My “Active Teammate” Experiment

Over the next few weeks, I will investigate the practical applications of OpenClaw to streamline my workflow. Using a dummy account to ensure data safety, I’ll be testing its ability to act as an “active teammate” in three key areas:

  • Email Triage and “Inbox Zero”: Can OpenClaw move beyond simple filters to autonomously scan, categorise, and archive thousands of unread emails based on context?
  • Intelligent Meeting Prep: By granting the agent access to my Calendar and Google Drive, I want them to review previous minutes and correspondence to draft briefing notes and discussion points for upcoming meetings.
  • LMS & Course Administration (The “Long Shot”): I am exploring how to integrate OpenClaw with Learning Management Systems to monitor student submissions and automatically dispatch personalised “check-in” reminders via Discord or WhatsApp. While technically complex, this could revolutionise student support.

posts.title: A Tale of Two Graduations: From South Africa to Hong Kong
posts.content:
Graduation ceremonies have a unique kind of magic, the kind that makes time pause and hearts swell with pride. Sitting in a Hong Kong university hall this week, watching students in crisp gowns and proud smiles, I found myself thinking back to another graduation, years ago, on a different continent.

When I was in South Africa, graduations carried a deep, almost sacred significance for many families. I remember seeing parents, often cleaners, gardeners, or drivers, finish their long shifts and walk straight to the campus, uniforms still on. Some would even take their work badges off and hand them to a co-worker or tuck them away, just to blend in among the guests and watch their sons or daughters take those triumphant steps toward the graduation hall.

It was humbling and powerful. Many of these young graduates were the first in their families, sometimes the first in their entire community, to earn a university degree. I will never forget the tears, the ululations, the way mothers waved proudly from the stands. Every step across that stage represented decades of struggle and perseverance made visible.In Hong Kong, the atmosphere is a little different. Here, education is deeply ingrained; many students are third or even fourth-generation graduates. The celebrations are quieter, the pride perhaps more subdued, but the feeling underneath is surprisingly familiar. Whether it’s a South African mother in her cleaner’s uniform or a Hong Kong father adjusting his son’s mortarboard, the emotion of seeing a child succeed is the same: joy, relief, and a deep sense of fulfillment.

Graduation, I realized, is not just an academic ritual; it’s a moment of human connection that transcends class and culture. Because behind every graduate, no matter where they are in the world, stands someone who dared to hope for a better future, and worked to make it possible.

posts.title: The Weight of Decision: My Experience as a University Admissions Interviewer
posts.content:
Last week marked a significant event in the lives of many young individuals in Hong Kong: the release of the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education (DSE) results. This period is crucial as it determines the next steps in their academic journeys, and for some, it might dictate their future careers. As a lecturer at a university, I, along with other staff members, was responsible for interviewing students to assess their suitability for admission. It was a task that gave me an unexpected power – the power to influence a student’s future. This power left me grappling with a myriad of emotions and ethical considerations.

As I sat in the interview room, watching each hopeful student walk in with anticipation and nervousness etched on their faces, I couldn’t help but question my own qualifications for this role. Who am I to decide who gets in or not? This question lingered in my mind throughout the process. The weight of my decisions was overwhelming, knowing that my judgment could significantly impact a student’s career path and, ultimately, their life.

The gravity of the situation became more apparent with each interview. Each student had a story, a dream, and a unique set of circumstances that brought them to this pivotal moment. It was a humbling experience, realising that my role in this process was not just about evaluating academic achievements but also about understanding the person behind the scores. I felt a deep sense of responsibility to be fair and just, to look beyond the numbers and see the potential within each individual.

However, as the interviews progressed, I noticed the inherent subjectivity in the process. Despite attempts to standardise the evaluation criteria, the human element in the interview process meant that biases and personal perceptions inevitably played a role. Hearing some of my colleagues mention that a candidate’s appearance could influence their decision was disconcerting. The notion that someone’s physical attractiveness could impact their academic future was troubling. It raised questions about the system’s fairness and whether true talent might be overlooked due to superficial judgments.

This subjectivity brought to light the broader issue of assessing potential and merit. While academic results measure a student’s capabilities, they do not capture the full picture. The interviews were supposed to fill that gap, but the process seemed flawed. The idea that appearance could sway decisions highlighted the need for a more objective and equitable approach to admissions.

Reflecting on this experience, I realised the importance of advocating for a more holistic and unbiased evaluation system. As educators, we have a duty to recognise and nurture potential, irrespective of superficial factors. The power to influence a student’s future should be wielded with great care, ensuring that our decisions are based on genuine merit and potential rather than personal biases.

The emotional toll of this responsibility was significant. Each rejection felt like a failure, a missed opportunity to support a student’s dream. The faces of the disappointed students haunted me long after the interviews ended. I questioned whether I had made the right choices and was fair and just in my evaluations. The pressure to make the right decision was immense, knowing that my judgment could alter the course of a young person’s life.

This experience also underscored the importance of empathy and compassion in the admissions process. Getting caught up in the numbers and criteria is easy, but we must remember that behind every application is a person with hopes, dreams, and aspirations. By approaching the interviews with empathy, we can better understand the context of each student’s achievements and challenges, making more informed and considerate decisions.

In conclusion, my experience as a university admissions interviewer was a profound and eye-opening journey. It made me acutely aware of the power and responsibility that comes with the role. It highlighted the need for a fair and unbiased admissions process that recognises true potential beyond superficial factors. As educators, we must strive to ensure that our decisions are guided by principles of equity and compassion, understanding the profound impact they have on the lives of our students. This experience has shaped my perspective on admissions and reinforced my commitment to fostering an inclusive and supportive academic environment where every student can succeed based on their true potential. I wish those who got the post all the best for this program, and for those who did not get the opportunity, your path may lie elsewhere.

posts.title: Supporting Students with Special Educational Needs: A Guide for Lecturers
posts.content:
As educators, our goal is to facilitate learning for all students, recognizing that each individual comes with unique strengths and challenges. Special Educational Needs (SEN) encompass a range of learning difficulties and disabilities that require special instructional strategies and accommodations to help students achieve their educational potential.

Understanding Special Educational Needs

Special Educational Needs can vary widely among students. Some may face physical disabilities that affect their mobility or dexterity, while others may have learning difficulties such as dyslexia or ADHD. There are also students who face sensory impairments or communication disorders that impact their ability to engage with traditional teaching methods. Recognizing the diversity within SEN is the first step toward effective support.

Role of a Lecturer in Supporting SEN Students

As a lecturer, your approach to students with SEN can significantly influence their educational outcomes. Here are several strategies to enhance your teaching to meet the needs of all learners:

  1. Personalized Learning Plans: Work with special education professionals to create or adapt learning plans that address the specific needs of SEN students. These plans should highlight areas that need accommodations, such as extended time for assignments, modified coursework, or alternative assessment methods.
  2. Inclusive Teaching Techniques: Employ teaching methods that are inclusive of all learning styles. This can include using visual aids, providing written and oral instructions, incorporating technology, and offering hands-on activities. Ensuring that your teaching materials are accessible to students with visual or hearing impairments is also crucial.
  3. Encourage Participation: Create a classroom environment where all students feel safe and encouraged to participate. This might involve group work that allows for peer support, as well as fostering an open dialogue where students feel comfortable expressing their needs and preferences.
  4. Ongoing Assessment and Feedback: Regularly assess the effectiveness of the accommodations and modify them as necessary. Feedback from SEN students is invaluable in this process. It’s important to have an open line of communication and to seek their input on what is working or what changes might be beneficial.
  5. Professional Development: Stay informed about the latest research and strategies in special education. Participating in workshops and training sessions on SEN can enhance your skills and provide you with new tools to better support your students.
  6. Collaboration with Colleagues: Work closely with other educators, counselors, and SEN specialists. Collaborative approaches can lead to more effective strategies for supporting students with diverse needs.

Conclusion

Supporting students with Special Educational Needs requires a thoughtful, personalized approach that respects each student’s individuality and promotes their academic success. As lecturers, our adaptability and willingness to learn new teaching methods play a crucial role in empowering all students to reach their fullest potential. Let’s commit to creating an educational environment that is inclusive, supportive, and conducive to learning for everyone.

posts.title: Dealing with Student Mental Health Crises During Examinations: Guidelines for Lecturers
posts.content:
Introduction

As educators, we’re not only tasked with imparting knowledge but also with supporting our students’ well-being. Recently, during a practice exam session, an incident occurred where a student experienced a significant mental health crisis, resulting in a two-hour delay and a challenging situation for all involved. This student did try to use this an emotional hostage to force the lecturer to pass “the student”. I feel we should respect the student, whether the student is trying to take advantage or not. Benefit of the doubt, the student had emotional and mental stress, and we should have empathy for them.

This blog aims to share insights and guidelines on how lecturers can effectively handle such situations to support the student in distress while maintaining a conducive exam environment.

Recognizing Signs of Distress

The first step in handling such crises is recognizing the signs of mental distress. Symptoms may include:

  • Unusual or erratic behavior
  • Inability to communicate coherently
  • Visible signs of panic or anxiety
  • Abrupt emotional responses

Immediate Steps to Take

  1. Ensure Safety: Ensure the safety of all students and staff in the room. This might involve calmly asking other students to leave the room if the situation escalates.
  2. Remain Calm: Your calm demeanor can have a soothing effect. Speak in a soft, gentle tone to reassure the student and those around.
  3. Provide Space: If possible, provide the student with some physical space. Crowding or too many interactions may increase their stress.
  4. Seek Professional Help: Contact campus security or health services for immediate assistance. They can help in managing the situation more professionally and provide the necessary medical or psychological aid.
  5. Postpone the Exam: Consider the wellbeing of the student as a priority. Depending on the severity of the incident, postponing or rescheduling the exam for the affected student may be necessary.

Communicating with the Student

  1. Show Empathy: Let the student know you are there to help, not to judge. Simple phrases like “I’m here to help,” or “I can see you’re really upset, let’s find a way to make you feel better,” can be comforting.
  2. Maintain Confidentiality: Respect the student’s privacy by not discussing the specifics of the incident with other students.

Follow-Up Actions

  1. Document the Incident: Record details of the event, including how it was handled and the outcome. This documentation can be crucial for follow-up actions and future reference.
  2. Support Services: Guide the student to appropriate university support services, such as counselling centers. Continuous support can help them manage their stress better in the future.
  3. Review Exam Policies: Reflect on the incident to see if there are ways to improve the handling of such situations in the future. This might involve setting up more robust support systems during exams or training staff on mental health first aid.

Conclusion

Handling a mental health crisis during an examination requires sensitivity, prompt action, and a focus on the well-being of all students. By following these guidelines, lecturers can help mitigate the impact of such crises and support their students’ mental health and academic success. Sharing these experiences and solutions increases awareness and preparedness, ultimately creating a more supportive educational environment.

posts.title: Navigating the Virtual World: A Comparison of HTC VR, Meta Quest 2, and Meta Quest 3 Pro
posts.content:
The world of virtual reality (VR) is evolving rapidly, offering ever more immersive and interactive experiences. Among the top contenders in this field are the HTC VR, Meta Quest 2, and the newly launched Meta Quest 3 Pro. Each of these headsets has its unique features and strengths, making them suitable for different users and purposes. Let’s take a closer look at each of these devices to help you decide which might be the best fit for your VR needs.

1. HTC VR: A Premium Experience for Enthusiasts

The HTC VR line, known for its high-end Vive series, offers a premium VR experience. The latest models come with cutting-edge technology, high-resolution displays, and a robust library of content. They are particularly favored by VR enthusiasts and professionals who require superior graphics and precision. However, this quality comes at a higher price point and often requires a powerful PC to run effectively, making it less accessible to casual users.

Key Features:

  • High-resolution displays for crystal clear visuals.
  • Advanced tracking and room-scale VR capabilities.
  • A strong focus on enterprise solutions and professional use.

2. Meta Quest 2: The Sweet Spot for Casual and Social VR

The Meta Quest 2, formerly known as the Oculus Quest 2, is a popular choice for its balance of affordability, performance, and ease of use. It’s a standalone headset, meaning it doesn’t require a PC or external sensors. The Quest 2 offers a wide variety of games and apps, making it ideal for casual gaming, social VR experiences, and media consumption. Its user-friendly interface and wireless design provide a great entry point for those new to VR.

Key Features:

  • Standalone, wireless operation for ease of use.
  • A diverse library of games and applications.
  • Competitive pricing, making it accessible to a broader audience.

3. Meta Quest 3 Pro: A Glimpse into the Future of VR

The Meta Quest 3 Pro is the latest offering, building on the success of the Quest 2. It’s designed to offer a more advanced VR experience, possibly incorporating features like enhanced graphics, improved tracking, and a more ergonomic design. While the specifics are still emerging, the Quest 3 Pro aims to bridge the gap between the casual and professional VR markets, offering high-end features at a relatively affordable price.

Key Features (Speculated):

  • Improved graphics and processing power.
  • Enhanced comfort and ergonomic design.
  • Advanced features for a more immersive experience.

Conclusion: Choosing the Right VR Headset for You

Choosing between the HTC VR, Meta Quest 2, and Meta Quest 3 Pro depends on your specific needs and budget. If you’re a VR enthusiast or professional seeking the highest quality experience, the HTC VR is a compelling choice. For those looking for a balance of price, performance, and ease of use, the Meta Quest 2 is a great option. And if you’re excited about the latest advancements in VR and are willing to invest a bit more, the Meta Quest 3 Pro could be the way to go.

As the VR landscape continues to evolve, each of these headsets offers a unique way to experience the virtual world, whether for gaming, socializing, or professional applications. The key is to consider what aspects of VR are most important to you and choose accordingly.

posts.title: Embracing the Future of Wireless VR: A Simple Guide to Setting Up Your Meta VR Headset
posts.content:
Virtual Reality (VR) has taken giant strides away from the clunky, wire-laden experiences of its infancy, evolving into an immersive blend of reality and digital excellence. Among the champions of this futuristic endeavor, the Meta VR headset stands out, particularly for its seamless setup process, which is reminiscent of today’s intuitive smartphone technologies. This wireless wonder, promising an untethered dive into the virtual realm, contrasts sharply with predecessors like the HTC VIVE, which often required a love for tech tinkering to get started.

If you’ve just got your hands on a Meta VR headset, congratulations are in order! You’re about to enter a world where the digital and physical realms coalesce in the most interactive way yet. Let’s walk you through the surprisingly easy setup process.

Unboxing the Future

First, the unboxing. Meta ensures that you’re not overwhelmed right from the get-go. Inside, you’ll find the VR headset, controllers, and all necessary charging equipment—a far cry from the jumble of cables and extensions that users of older systems like the HTC VIVE might expect.

Step into the New World: Setting Up

  1. Charge Up: Begin by charging your headset and controllers. Just like your cellphone, you’ll want ample juice to get through those initial hours of awe.
  2. Download the Meta App: While your headset is powering up, download the Meta mobile app from your smartphone’s app store. This acts as your command center, akin to handling a smart device.
  3. Create or Log into Your Account: If you’re new to Meta, you’ll need to set up an account. If you already have one, simply log in. This account is a passport to your virtual experiences.
  4. Pair Your Headset: Once your headset is charged, put it on. You’ll be guided through a series of simple on-screen prompts for initial setup, including connecting to your Wi-Fi. The headset’s UI is designed to be as user-friendly as a smartphone, so follow along, and you’ll be fine.
  5. Bluetooth Magic: Next, pair your controllers using Bluetooth via the on-screen instructions. The lack of wires is a real game-changer, as it allows for unencumbered movement, enhancing your immersion.
  6. Define Your Space: Safety first! You’ll need to define your ‘Guardian’ boundaries to prevent real-world obstacles from spoiling your VR fun. The headset will help you with this, ensuring you know the limits of your physical space while you’re lost in the virtual one.
  7. Dive In!: With the technicalities sorted, it’s time to dive in. Use your app or the headset’s virtual library to download games, apps, and experiences. Before you know it, you’ll be exploring new worlds, playing incredibly immersive games, or interacting with others in a virtual space.

A New Reality Unveiled

The beauty of the Meta VR headset lies not just in its advanced technology providing high-quality immersive experiences but also in its accessibility. It’s a device that welcomes rather than intimidates, much like how modern cellphones do. Its wireless nature, coupled with a UI that echoes the ease of a smartphone, marks a significant turn in making cutting-edge tech accessible and enjoyable for the masses.

As you embark on your virtual journeys, remember that the Meta VR headset is more than a gadget; it’s a portal to new realms. Enjoy the ride!

My Experience with the Alienware M15 R2 and HTC VIVE COSMO Setup

In 2020, I had the incredible opportunity to acquire the Alienware M15 R2 laptop, a beast in its time and arguably even now. Although the gaming world has evolved rapidly since then, especially with powerhouses like the ROG ALLY, some might argue that the Alienware M15 R2 has become somewhat dated. But let’s dive into the specifics.

Specifications:

  • Processor: Intel i7 9th-9750H Gen @ 2.6Ghz
  • RAM: 16GB
  • Storage: SSD 256GB
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 2070

For this venture, I paired my laptop with the HTC VIVE COSMO – a potent combo for any VR enthusiast.

But it’s not all about the hardware; the setup process deserves its fair share of spotlight. The initial step, which required a mini-display port, proved a challenge. Adapters for such aren’t just readily available in SA; you’d likely have to order one, and waiting can be rather tiresome.

Once all the gadgets were in hand, the real setup began. Excitement bubbling, I dove into the world of VR, only to be told there was too much light or the visuals needed tweaking. Patience truly is a virtue here.

Breaking down the setup time:

  • Software Installation: Roughly 2 hours.
  • Physical Environment Preparation: Approximately 15 minutes. (A necessary safety measure to avoid any potential mishaps.)
  • HTC VIVE Virtual Environment Configuration: About 30 minutes.

Of course, don’t forget about game and application downloads, which can vary based on your internet speed.

Summing it all up, the entire setup took me around 3.5 hours. Quite the commitment, but was it worth it? Absolutely. However, now I’m curious – how does this setup time compare to the Oculus? Lucky for me (and you, dear readers), I’ve got one on hand. Stay tuned for that comparison in a future post!

posts.title: What you need to succeed?
posts.content:
Hello there,

This is going to be a short post. I realize everyone has their own time for epiphanies. Mine to this, was today.

If you ask the big question “how can we become successful?”. Many would reply: KNOWLEDGE, some would say HARD-WORK. But what if none of these gives you success?

Does not make sense right? How can neither KNOWLEDGE nor HARD-WORK result in success? The answer is simple. Let us play a game, if each letter of the alphabet is replaced with a number that represents its position, eg: A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, etc…

KNOWLEDGE then becomes (11+14+15+23+12+5+4+7+5) = 96%
HARD-WORK then becomes (8+1+18+4+23+15+18+11) = 98%

Interestingly, neither of them gives you 100%, meanwhile if ATTITUDE is spelt out the same way…

ATTITUDE becoming (1+20+20+9+20+21+4+5) = 100%.

Not sure if this is a coincidences or not, but having the right attitude to start off and finish with is important. That is one of the biggest determining factor. Of course, I think having knowledge and being a hard-worker also contributes to being successful, but more importantly, having a positive and strong attitude is important. In this case, more important.

Keep well, and be strong.

posts.title: The road of PhD
posts.content:
Hi, how are you doing? I have written in a while, so I thought I’ll start now. Yes, I don’t want to do my work, so I’m going to do something that is somewhat work enhancing, which is… writing.

I just wanted to write something, and this will probably end up being very short. When people say the road of the PhD is very long and lonely, I thought, arg, whatever, it’s hate talk etc. But now that I am in it, I am thinking it is a lonely road, and it feels like I’m writing and writing like pore water into a toilet, I don’t know how much or when it’ll be full.

I won’t say it’s lonely, but it’s a lost journey. In comparison to a Masters, there is even less structure, even less guidelines. It is like the supervisor saying, go explore and do what you feel your heart desires. But, we will regulate you if you go over board. These regulations will shatter your ideas and goals. Not because they are not good enough, it is because they are too good, it’s like a dream, an un-graduatable dream.

“Lets get the degree over and done with, then you can start with your dream-research.” I understand that, I started off with a big project, and now, it is really small, somewhat linked to what I want to do, but not quite. Nevertheless, I will keep moving. I mean, let me keep moving…

See you around…

今天我想写关于我做的工作的表现和感觉。 我之前说过如何变强自己， 但是同时也要学习如何安慰自己。

昨天对于我工作的水平明显的下降了。我一天有大概17 – 18 件要处理的事， 但是很多更工作无关。 假如：看新闻， 写作十五分钟，做运动之类的。 这些我一天都能实现， 只是有时候没时间。 我的列表每天都要做十二样， 这才叫完成了一天。

之前我倒是觉得没问题， 因为天天都可以， 但是大学现在要在四月二十号开始上课了， 我们也要慢慢开始准备课了。 可能是之前太辛福了， 昨天，我好像忙了一天， 但一件事都没干。 感觉特别不好， 这种什么都没做感觉特别难受。这种内疚的感觉还影响到我跟家人的接触。 我昨天去运动了， 也好像没有什么心情。 我今天为什么要写这些呢？因为我想分享一下我怎么度过的。

我们给我们自己设定目标， 天天忙着工作， 盲目的工作， 有时候忙呀忙，回头一看， 好像什么都没干。 面对这样的情况我们第一要做的事就是接受我们有时候状态会不好。就像跑步一样， 有时候跑得快， 有时候跑得慢。 这都是事实， 我一开始也说了， 也要学会安慰自己。 怎么安慰， 要看你自己， 说了好像没说的一样， 我指的是：每个人安慰自己的方法都不一样，所以要看自己。我昨天运动了， 陪我家人看了一下电视， 脑海里还是会像关于没完成的工作， 之后把我没干好的重新看了一遍， 安排了今天要做一些什么，之后放下了让好往前看了，工作就这样结束了。

我能做出这样的时候， 已经完了，那时候我都回房间了，我爸妈也睡了晚上十点多了。 这一天还是浪费了。

其实什么都没做的一天也很正常。 我们要学会接受这些，不要再停留在过去， 我们要往前看， 怎么能不这些不影响到我们的今天和明天。更不能让这些事情影响到我们的家人和工作后的娱乐。 这样是不健康的。

今天， 很巧也是什么都没做的一天， 我很多目标都没达到.， 但是感觉明显的不一样。 我今天五点就“下班了” 运动了， 现在也陪我爸妈看电视剧。 刚觉很轻松。 在我看电视剧的时候我的导师给我的论文回信了， 说很多地方都写的不好要改。 看到的时候， 就会想，又来了， 有一堆事。 解决方法：把“改论文” 写到我的列表上，奇妙的事来了；这种烦恼就没有了。 我就开始写blog， 同时陪我爸妈看电视剧,看了三小时了。

没干什么活不是罪，不用“惩罚”自己，也不用感觉内疚。重新安排， 明天再来。 我倒是觉得当工作不顺利的时候，不要强逼自己继续，而是要停下来看看能改什么， 或者停一下， 出去走走， 看看外面， 放松一下。 这样才能达到目标，继续往前。却记，“懒”和“工作不顺利”有很大的差别的。 自己要分清楚哦， 怎么分？这个你问一下自己就清楚了。

我就写到这里了， 希望你工作一切顺利， 好好加油！下次见。 非

posts.title: Why I like talking
posts.content:
I am an extrovert, so they say. Well, I do admit that I get energy by doing fun and stressful things. It was made quite clear to me, I was the MC of my brothers wedding, oh boy, did I enjoy that. The busy-ness, behind the scene organizing, setting up, solving possible problems before it happens.

I actually wanted to write about something more serious, but for today, let me just settle with something simple. So I have been told many times, that those that talk much are those who do little, I may disagree with this, because I think it refers to the situation. If it’s in a meeting, maybe that is correct, but if you’re referring to a personal character, then it might not all be correct.

Talking helps me understand and figure things out, like some staying in a room and internally digesting something, I prefer speaking to people about it. You can imagine how my PhD supervisor will hate me right? Every time I have an idea, I would just want to go crazy and chat to them about it. That is a joke, because both my supervisors are professors, and they are indeed, quite busy.

So, why do I like talking? I personally think it is because it is how humans are different from others. And we should communicate to ensure there is no miss understanding. I talk to anyone, anytime and anywhere. I once watched a series where a casual citizen wanted to apply for a job, and needed to be a negotiator. This negotiator was a profession that worked with the police force to speak to criminals, psychological patients, mentally unstable citizens.

In one of the scenes, during he’s interview, he was required to speak about a watch. Although he knew nothing about a watch, the was able to speak about it, and link that to many other new topics, which eventually got him the job. I of course am not apply for any job, but I admire the ability to keep conversations going, and I think it is important for us to be able to do so. Whether it is professionally or personally. And the only way of getting this write is by talking, getting ideas and catching on what the person is saying and find their interest to spark more conversation.

If you have the ability to be able to spark up conversations, it’s better than struggling to think of something when it happens. Nevertheless, I just want to be able to make conversation with every one that I come across, as I feel there is a story that one wants to talk about in everyone.

posts.title: 每天变强 –
posts.content:
今天我想写的是， 四个让你自己变强的点。 这五个我还在磨练呢。

第一： 每天锻炼。
其实很简单， 能不能变强就要看你能不能自律。 因为很多时候我们输在三分钟热度， 坚持不到最后就放弃了。 所以， 天天锻炼是一个很好的开始。 我朋友曾经跟我说过，吃饭， 运动， 都是我们能控制， 但很难控制。假如我们这些能控制的因数都控制不了的话，生活凭什么让我们过的轻松呀。 所以，先来个控制运动， 保持天天运动的习惯。

第二： 习惯孤独。
这个对某些人来说也很简单， 但是有些人就很难。 这道题不用解释的那么多， 人会寂寞， 会想找人陪， 等你真的能自己跟自己过的时候， 不需要被人给你快乐， 你已经变强了。 我们都知道， 依赖别人不好。 为什么？因为凡事都要靠自己，对你“重要”的事情不代表对“别人”也那么重要。

第三： 读书吧。
我不喜欢读书， 而因为这点我的语言很差， 我经常没词， 或者词量很少。 我爸妈说的对， 读书永远都是好事。 其实真的， 读什么都会帮得了你， 因为你会长知识，当然我指的是书。很多事都有理论，解答一些你现在有的问题。 你可以问，我也很想都书， 但是就坚持不了，那我个人觉得是因为你读的那本书不是你喜欢的类型。打个比方， 就像运动，或者做数学题。你要是喜欢打羽毛球的，不管你多菜， 你也会打， 同时， 你厉害， 你也会喜欢。 相反， 你要是不喜欢或者水平不好， 你怎么打， 你也不会想继续。 所以第一步， 找到你喜欢的。

第四： 情绪
对， 我们人类都是情绪化动物， 什么决定都会有一些情绪在里头。 同时， 别人也很影响到你的情绪。不管你是什么人，你的情绪都会被别人而影响。 我老师跟我说过，人为什么会生气？因为你把别人犯的错，放在你自己身上了。你对这个人做的事情或者说的话不满， 而他什么都没感觉都，却让你情绪化了。 少生气，生身体。 这句话我们都知道， 但是很难做的好。 如果你每次都在为别人生气， 或者想着别人怎么怎么样， 你不妨可以这样想： 如果这个人做的，说的， 不影响你（1）财经状况, (2)健康和人身安全， (3) 家人， 管他说啥， 做啥。 对吧？ 就好像你买了件新的衣服，第一次穿， 你以为大家都会看到你买的， 穿的新衣服，但其实没有。因为在这个世界上，除非你是名人，高端， 没有人会瞅你一眼。 为什么？因为没时间，我们不嫌。 所以， 别再为那些人做的，说的不开心或者生气。 因为你也没时间。

本来还有一个的， 但是想不出来。 看看晚点会不会想起来， 再加上去吧。 先这样， 拜拜。

posts.title: Discovery Product Review Two
posts.content:
Let me continue with this chapter. I think it is important to thinking about what you really want regarding this membership.

The additional benefits you can get is the money back counter. You can choose from a various amount of stores like, Woolworth, Pick ‘n Pay, Total Sports, Sportsman warehouse, etc. It is important to see where you spend your money, because once you select, you cannot change it. Ie: If you shop more at Pick ‘n Pay, don’t choose Woolworth, because the percentage of return is different.

Lastly, the flight, hotel and car rentals. There is some discount here, of course, it’s not the best, but it’s not bad on good timing deals. Although, the booking cannot be simultaneous. Meaning you cannot book a car for today and expect a discount. I cannot remember how long it must be prior your bookings, so it’s best to figure that out and plan ahead. Although sometimes it’s cheaper booking one way with the discounted flights from Discovery, and another (return) from another company, like SAFair.

iWatch, Shoe boaster and watch boasters. Of course being with discovery, you would want to purchase your apple or non apple sport watch. What is nice is that Discovery allows you to buy any of them, what you have to do is pay up front, and then Discovery will pay you every month, back. You have to review your status to see how much you limit is, IE: they don’t pay more than R2500.00, so if you buy a 6k watch, they only going to pay you 2.5k back (well, 2.5 / 12 = 208 pm). So before you sink in to pay that, you must be careful.

Additionally, you don’t have to buy the watch, but you can get a pair of shoes. This is also something you have to work out. What is the maxim price of the shoe you can get. If I have the time, I will list this is my next blog post, to make things easier.

If you’re planning to get the shoe and an non-apple sport watch, sad news for you, you cannot. You can only have one boaster activated at a time. With that being said, there are different categories of boasters. There are four boaster categories, Bike Boaster, non-apple watch and shoe boaster, apple watch boaster and gym boaster. These above mentioned four, you can have simultaneously. For example, I have Shoe, apple watch and gym boaster active all at once. If I cycled, I would have used that boaster too, but sadly, I don’t.

Apple watches. I know they are VERY expensive, but it’s cheap with discovery. But they bind you to a credit card, which means more payments. Eg: bank fees and monthly costs. But of course it still works out cheaper than buying it on contract or cashing it out. I personally have also shifted to discovery banking, and car insure (Which I will also write about soon).

Now, if you activated all these boasters, how do you make sure you don’t pay this back. It’s actually very simple, you need to ensure you reach all your goals. How do you reach your goals? Well, it depends how active you are. Your active goals goes as follows:

*60% heart rate for an hour gets you 100 points

*70% of your heart rate for 30 minutes gets you 200 points

*70% of your heart rate for an hour gets you 300 points

*80% of your heart rate gets you 300 points

How do you work out your maximum heart rate? Take (220 – your age) x 0.80. So for example: I am 30, 220 – 30 = 190 x 0.8 = 152 beats per minutes. Meaning to get 300 points I must get an average of 152 beats per minute for a period of 30 minutes to get my 300 points.

Getting 152 is a little impossible for you? Well, stay connected, I’ll tell you the ways you can get points!

posts.title: 待办事项列表 – A to do list
posts.content:
大家好， 现在是南非封城的时候， 睡都不能出门。 因为这个， 我们被逼着在家工作， 那这个话题就来了。 工作的环境变了， 我们怎么去改变我们的工作环境， 让这个病毒不影响我们。

我最近一直在想， 我为什么工作效率不好， 但是怎么找， 这不知道原因。 后来发现是因为我东西太多了， 我的列表太满了。 不知道该从何起。

我想介绍一下， 改变我的工作效率就是一个APP 叫 ToDoist. 我是苹果粉， 但是还是记得苹果自带的不是太好用。 没有对比， 就没有伤害。

我想说说苹果自带的事什么， 在比较一下ToDoist。 苹果的列表什么都有。 可以设成今天，还有全部。 可以加棋 （重要的） 最好的是， 可以分享（苹果）当然也可以添加自己的列表。 但是这些都没什么。 我就的都是基本的。

ToDoist的话， 就有点不一样了。 除了分享一样的列表给别人， 上面的都有。 而且，你可以设计一天做都少个项目。 比如说： 一天 五个。 等你做完五个的时候， 他会写“恭喜， 大盗目标了”。 你可能觉得这个没啥， 但是当你忙了一天， 但是感觉好像什么都没干的时候， 这个小小的鼓励会给你打来快乐。 因为他是告诉你， 你今天又干活，不是白干的。

还有一个就是， 你可以把今天没写完了，或者没干完的，挪到明天。 不同颜色代表时间点 （今天， 明天，七天之后， 全部）。我觉得这样挺好的， 因为你可以更细节的计划你每周想做的事。 目前为止还不错， 但是我回去上班之后可能就不一样。 我现在写的都是我现在在家的感受。

有另外一个功能是， 你能看到一周里头， 那天你完成了最多项目。 假如说， 周一对我来说最差， 因为一般回邮件就会用半天。 周二周三好很多， 因为可以开始干我想做的事了。 同时你也可以看到你每天能不能达到目标。 我之前看到一个视频， 他说， 如果你想做好一件事， 或者像变的更好， 就要天天做。让“他” 变成你吃饭上班的样子。 所以我的列表加了几个我天天都要做的事： 看新闻， 看汇率， 做俯卧撑， 做仰卧起坐， 每天写15分钟Blog 还有 博士论文。 我的列表每天底线是 九件事。 每天都要做九件。 做了上面的， 就已经六件了。

最后一个我喜欢的是， 每次你完成了一件任务的时候， 你都会积分。 虽然我不知道一件会积累都少分数， 但是看到自己的分数一天一天的增加， 还是不错的。 我们都知道列表是一个装不满的马桶.天天都有跟多的任务，事情要处理， 所以看到慢慢积累的分数， 真的很有成就感。

ToDoist 简单版是免费的。 你也可以付费。 不贵。 但是对我来说，简单版已经勾勒。 我一开始不是太想用的三着的APP， 我觉得苹果是最好的， 但是很多我喜欢的功能， 苹果都没有。 还是用ToDoist。

希望以上能帮到你更轻松的工作。 不要更努力工作， 要学的聪明点。 加油！

posts.title: Windows to Mac V1.0?
posts.content:
Hi all, so today I will talk about what the feeling was when moving from Windows to Mac.

I have been using Windows for all of my life. I was one of those who always spoke bad about apple, and not used it. I know all the short cuts on windows, the way it works and function etc. But the one down thing about windows is that, the laptop needs replacement, or formatting ever so often.

And, when you’re a junior, you have all the time to do so. Changing parts, troubleshooting which component of the computer is not working. But as time goes by, you just need your technology to work. Life is stressful enough already, and a not working PC, is worse.

I have been using apple, since 2015, and today, I feel like an apple collector. I won’t talk good about apple, and I won’t talk good about window either. I am here today to speak about the feeling of transit that I went through from going window to mac.

At first, frustration, anger, unhappiness, tricked and deceived. Before anything experiences (like a Mac book Air) you would read reviews. I read good and bad reviews, but none talks about the transfer from window to mac. And now, I’m going to talk about.

It took me almost a month to get used to the function and shortcuts. First things first, the mac is beautiful, but is it good in function?

(1) the keyboard layout is different. Control, alt and windows key, are all relocated to another location. My pinky being a strong finger from all the control-ing is now just shifting. I guess the point of mac is meaningful, as our thumb is stronger than our pinky. Nevertheless, it took some time to get used to the keyboard. Then the short cut, the short cuts concepts are the same, but the keys are different. The one that took me the longest to figure out was “delete” and “copy and pasting”.

Moving on, there is no more “menu” where all your software is stored. So everything are “apps” now, no longer having software. Of course the concept is still the same, you install software like how you install “apps” on your phone.

SPACE! Space is limited and very expensive, I had to buy an expansion SD card for this (which is another conversation, but have a look, this is what I bought for my Mac Book Air). I really struggled with space, moving from an 1TB SSD to a 128 SSD, okay, the speed was better, but it took sometime to get used to the fact that you can no longer just “keep things” around. High capacity items like movies and pictures, I had to remove or move to the SD Card. I guess you could carry a hard drive to assist with the space issue, but being a apple person, the whole point is actually minimalist (which you will soon realize, it’s not true.), well to a certain extent.

Next, software and drivers. It took me forever to setup my printer, because I couldn’t, or better yet, don’t know how to find the drive for Mac and install it. And no, I’m not computer literate. Anyhow, it worked at the end, but you really would struggle if you don’t have the time to figure all of this out.

Desktop, desktop and desktop. This is where I think it’s debatable, apple has many “desktops” where windows only have one, with many “blocks” where you can drag and it sits. Apple makes it easier for you to multitask by having multiple desktops that you have swipe left and right, which is nice, until you need to read and write, this is where window excel. Yes, yes, I know that Mac can have split window, but it’s easier on a window PC than a Apple. But there is a work around, you can install a third party app (which again takes time to read up and figure out).

posts.title: 泡泡泡， 泡咖啡
posts.content:
哈咯， 我之前说过， 我每天都要写点东西的， 由于我是个中国人， 我想我该写点中文吧。 所以， 一天中文， 一天英文。

最近南非再封城，你可能知道， 也可能不知道， 很多国家都在封城。 总共是21天， 今天是十三天。 可以说我这十三天一天都没出去过， 挺好的， 在家呆着。 有时候会有点无聊， 那又怎么样呢， 对吧？总比感染病毒好呀。

哪， 我们在家都干啥呀？ 我这个人比较喜欢喝咖啡， 我也开了个blog有关南非的不同咖啡点。 虽然不多， 但是这是要慢慢的积累， 对不对？ 今天我想写的就是怎么去泡备好的咖啡。我中文不是那么号， 可能会用一些英语来代替。

需要准备的东西： 咖啡Plunger (柱塞)， 咖啡粉（或者咖啡豆， 但是你需要磨成粉）， 杯子，热水和奶。

可以先烧水，之后把杯子和柱塞洗干净。记得，咖啡跟吃的很像， 要看和的那个人的口味。 所以， 选择好的咖啡粉和咖啡豆是很重要的。 我在这就现在就不说怎么去买咖啡豆， 这个我下回再说。

热水先把杯子柱塞泡热， 把水倒掉之后把咖啡粉倒到柱塞里再倒热水。又搪瓷搅匀， 搅个一分钟吧，再慢慢的把柱塞的盖子放上。让味道喝水混在一起，也同时让咖啡粉沉下去。

过了大概三到四分钟再把柱塞的盖子咬下去， 记得要慢慢压。我个人觉得下放热牛奶，再放咖啡比较好，但是这也看个人了。

这样就好了！ 哈哈。 简单不？

posts.title: Discovery Product Review one
posts.content:
Discovery has been around for many years, and of guilt, I have not been to active regarding using their products. Their apple watch with active goals has been around since 2015?

Disclaimer:
Before I continue, please note that Discovery has not paid me to do any of this, I am just doing this for the sake of writing and telling the whole the experience that I had by using their products, so whether it’s a good or bad experience it is not because someone asked or paid me to do it.

I signed up for Discovery’s product sign March 2019, by the end of October, I changed my car insurance, bank and signed up for their gym. To be honest, I don’t really know whether to start, but like all games, we have to start somewhere, let’s talk about one of the more well known items on the list: Discovery and Gym membership.

Discovery and Virgin Active:

So, you first need to be part of their Discovery Medical Aid program to be able to activate this benefit. There is an activation fee involved, and like all things, we have a heat period of 3 minutes, where we will be frantic about this “new product” and then it becomes “boring”. So before signing for gym, yes, I know its very exciting and it “motivates” you, but if you don’t have a habit of going to gym or exercising before signing, then you probably shouldn’t. Nevertheless, I signed up only to realize that it bonds you to a year contract, meaning any cancellation to policy will result in fines.

Also, if you have done your research, there are different packages that you can sign up for. (1) off peak, (2) All day, one gym, (3) anywhere any time. Obviously the cost changes based on the package you choose. For me? I chose (3) anywhere anytime, because I could go shower in any gym, work out based on where I worked etc. It was all fun, soon to realize that gym actually takes a lot of time, a 30 minute session (required by discovery) actually takes about an hour.

What do I mean?
Well, you get to gym, park, get changed and then warm up + gym (40-45 minutes) then cool down (5 minutes) and then you have about 10 minutes to shower and get ready. Altogether takes about an hour. It’s all good if you don’t have to go anywhere, you just pack your things and go home. But what I’m saying is, there is no “quick” workout. Additionally, you still have the issue of “gym fear”, meaning fear to do something because you think someone is watching you.

posts.title: Tips when travelling to China
posts.content:
Introduction

Ever since the 70’s China has opened it doors for foreigner to travel in and out of China, but as you may have heard, China is a developing country, which means there may her hurdles that one may need to overcome.

I have been in China myself for a new times, and over the course of these years, I have compiled a list of things at which I think will be helpful for those travelling to China for the first time.

Cash is King:

With the modern day technology, cash has been replaced with cards and applications, which is true in China as well. They use a system called WeChat Pay. South Africa once tried this initiative, but soon was dropped due to the decrease in popularity. Although the opposite is true in China. everyone there uses WeChat Pay.

Well, that’s contradictory to the heading yes?

That is because in order to use WeChat Pay in China, you first need the Chinese Currency, which is RMB (Ren Min Bi), AKA the Chinese Yuan. In addition to having the currency you also need to have a bank account with one of the local Chinese Banks. Meaning it’s a lot of effort for using WeChat Pay for the short duration that you’re going to be there. Hence, Cash is King.

Communication Platforms

It is important to note that China has banned google, you can read more about it here. But sadly, all google services are suspended. Meaning, Gmail, Google search, Google Drive and Play store. A good alternative would be creating an Outlook account, and forward all your emails to your outlook account so you can still access newly sent emails while you’re in China. If you don’t know how to forward your Gmails to your new email account, please have a look here.

In addition to google, other social media are also restricted, such as Facebook, Instagram, whats app. For other websites, have a look here.

With problems, there are always solutions. Microsoft’s Gurdeep Singh-Pall created something called the Virtual Private Network (VPN). VPN allows users to connect to networks around the world as if their device is connected or plugged into the hub. Below is a list of 2019 Free VPN applications that one can get before travelling to China.

  1. Hotspot Shield gives users 500 MB of data every day for free
  2. Windscribe gives free account holders 10 GB of data for free each month
  3. bVPN provides 30 minutes of free browsing per day
  4. hide.me offers 2 GB of data and 3 servers for free users
  5. TunnelBear offers GhostBear to help you bypass China’s firewall

Exchanging money:

Correct me if I am wrong, but once you have left the major city or airport, exchanging money is an issue.

Assuming you have travelled internationally, it would be best to grab some US Dollars (USD) with you before you arrive, that way it will be easier to exchange your USD into RMB at your arrival.

If you’re needing a guideline for exchanges and trends, XE is a good one to use. It takes the average of the buying and selling the currency. Of course, these numbers are optimistic, it will be difficult to get the exact rates displayed on XE.

Besides exchanging at the airport or Forex, you can also draw cash at the ATM, but that of course have costs involved, at which you may be charge from both your local bank and the Chinese Bank.

Time Difference

The time zone changes as you fly towards the Chinese Country. China is about six hours a head of time. Eg: If you’re in China 07h00, it would be South Africa’s 02h00.

Therefore, just be aware if someone does not reply you as you may be texting in the early morning.

Internet

Internet is freely accessible in China, but there is a requirement. You need a cellphone number. Most of the free WiFi in China requires you to enter your local Chinese CellPhone number. Therefore do not be surprised when they ask you to enter your cellphone number.

WiFi is a good limitless solution, but we also have 4G (or 5G coming soon). The two major cellular provider is: China Telecom and China Unicom. You may be able to purchase these SIM cards at the airport or at the corner shop. Do get someone who understands the bundles to go with you. Because there are a lot of bundles that you can purchase. Eg: Netflix bundle (in South African content) 20GB for 50 Yuan.

That is very cheap for watching series etc, but that bundle does not include everyday mobile data. IE: your WeChat app or whats app application will not run from that data, so you will have to buy additional data to use the social networking applications.

Adapters

Please have a look at the adapter used in China. It is a little different to other countries, therefore it would be advisable for you to bring along an adapter for you to charge and use your electronic devices.

Safety and scams

China is a very safe country. But caution should be taken where ever you go. Pick pocketing and scamming is common in China. If something is too good to be true, it probably is.

Walking around in China at night is fine, but still be alert and aware of your surrounding. Travel in groups, I guess the normal protocol should be observed.

Transportation

There are many ways of travelling in China.

  • Di Di Taxi (Uber)
  • Public bus
  • Tax
  • Walking
  • Public Bicycle

These way of transports can be used at your convenience, with a cost involved of course.

Chinese Currency

I think it might be important for you to be familiar with what the notes looks like from the Chinese Currency.

  • 100 yuan – Red
  • 50 yuan – Dark Green
  • 20 yuan – Brown
  • 10 yuan – Light blue
  • 5 yuan – Purple
  • 1 yuan – Light Green

Conclusion

Hope you enjoyed this little heads up blog. There are many things that one could consider as a hurdle, but I think it is also a good thing for you to experience it yourself.

Most of all, enjoy your trip!

posts.title: China Hong Kongand Taiwan in South Africa
posts.content:
I should start with an introduction about myself, otherwise, this post would not make sense. My name is Tak Wing with a surname of YU. I was born in Hong Kong and moved to South Africa before 1997, and ever since, I have lived here as a South African.

I am not sure how clued up you are about the history of China and Hong Kong, but if you’re interested in reading up a little about it, you can find it here. All in all, Hong Kong became the Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China. Meaning “一国两制” which means “One country, two systems”. If I were to explain that, pages here will not be enough, but in a nutshell, basically the government in China cannot have a say in what happens in Hong Kong, yet Hong Kong is part of China and is influenced by China. The topic I want to speak about is the differences in culture and also the hate or misleading thoughts of people from China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.

Now first, you will have to understand that there is a “dislike” attitude and emotions of which the Taiwanese and Hong Kongers have against the Chinese (mainland). For example, if a Chinese (mainland) goes to Hong Kong for shopping, the attitude they receive will be different based on their ascent of the language, Mandarin. The Taiwanese and Hong Konger will get superb services, where the Chinese will get a poorer and somewhat negative attitude.

I have been in South Africa for nearly 21 years, during the first 17 years, I have refused and rejected any communication and contact with Chinese people. I will not step into a Chinese Resturant or shop unless it’s owned by Taiwanese or a Hong Konger. If you can understand that someone 11 230 km away from China can still have this stereotype and attitude towards the Chinese, image the magnitude in China and Hong Kong. I must confess that this attitude is not without reason. The Chinese (some) has really poor respect for people and the environment. This boils down the civilization. Some Chinese can really be uncivilized.

Consequently, there has always been a separation between the Chinese and the Hong Konger and Taiwanese. If I were to explain the relationship in an equation it would look something like this:

Yes, it is true the Chinese are isolated by the Hong Kongers and the Taiwanese. Furthermore, the opposite is true, the Hong Kongers and Taiwanese are closer. This was my exact thought during the 17 years of living in South Africa, I had mostly Taiwanese friends and even had a Taiwanese girlfriend. Fortunately, I have been given the opportunity to change and embrace my culture by experiencing and learning the way of Chinese. In 2015 I met people from China, yes, like before, I would refuse to communicate, but we played a similar sport, badminton. Over a period of time, I found myself befriending them. From this, I learned, dealt and embraced them into my life and I saw I was more Chinese than I was Taiwanese and Hong Kongese. I enjoy my time with my Chinese people and started visiting China every year, trying to explore a different kind of China. One of my hights was the Great Wall of China. I eventually felt that being Chinese and not having been to the Great Wall is an insult to myself as a Proudly Chinese.

It was sad because, from 2015, I lost most of my Taiwanese friends. We drifted further and further apart, resulting all my Asian friends being mostly Chinese. It was the sad truth, but I felt like this was not my fault, I feel the misleading information given from our previous generation was the issue. Now that I am in the Chinese circle, I feel it was unfair that the Hong Kongese and Taiwanese had such an attitude against the Chinese. At the end of the day, we are all Chinese. We should unite and not have internal separation.
